aggregates.claim: A finite ledger over the exact current collected suite, with every execution ID, primary requirement, input/profile fingerprint, current adjudication, declared phase and evidence class bound into the inventory review. Inventory adjudication is distinct from case approval: explicit current needs-oracle or disputed members remain listed, unapproved and ineligible for qualified passes. Unreviewed, stale or falsely labelled reference evidence cannot be silently adopted. Declared-valid runtime effects, other effects, positive admission controls, undefined-result contexts and invalid-input diagnostics have separate populations. Actual observations are joined by exact ID and compiler configuration without adding an execution or attributing a canonical case to this requirement.
aggregates.limitation: Observational infrastructure only: S4.2-001's facet remains pending until the source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/oracle inventory and separate processor/dependency qualifications are independently established. No finite run proves the universal processor obligation. A filtered invocation retains all unselected members in its denominator. XFAILs remain failures; skips, unsupported modes, missing profiles, unavailable launchers, unexecuted run effects and provisional observations cannot become qualified passes. A compile/link admission is not execution of an interpretation, and a context-only run is not an assertion about an undefined value. Resource failures do not establish permitted size/complexity limits. Compiler headers, companions, launchers and profile observations describe the selected interface, not ABI certification or universal portability. Paragraphs 7-8 are recommendations, not manufactured mandatory documentation requirements.

review.rationale: Renewal of the whole-suite execution inventory after the exact-arithmetic FIXTURE packet in doc/source_audits/batch_119.json. The member count moves from 2089 to 2102 because this packet adds thirteen executable cases; authored_facets moves 1794 to 1807, pending facets 5090 to 5077, and fixture review states 1776 to 1789 reference-validated with 274 source-reviewed and 1 needs-oracle unchanged. The full suite is 972 tests, OK. All 2047 raw reviews, 263 catalogues, 22 links, R402 and the b153c75b baseline remain exact, and tests/expected_failures.txt is unchanged. These two subclauses were chosen because the batch101 review singled them out as the part of the numeric and character material that is genuinely portable: everything around them is hedged, since 7.4.3 makes real and complex values approximations and 10.1.5.2.4 permits any mathematically equivalent alternative, but integer division and concatenation are exact. Non-vacuity was proved by mutation rather than inspection, with twenty-eight numeric literals perturbed, nine character literals altered at equal length, three kind expectations, thirteen completion tokens, an operand-order swap and a changed LEN assertion, all failing as required. One mutation survived and is recorded rather than glossed: appending a trailing blank to an expected character literal survives for all nine character value assertions, because character comparison blank-pads the shorter operand. That is non-blocking only because each value comparison is paired with an explicit LEN assertion and with test-module content pins, so a wrong length is still caught; the value comparison alone would not catch it. On the decisive question for integer division, only two of the four fixtures distinguish the standard's truncation toward zero from the common wrong implementation of flooring, namely the negative-dividend case where minus eight divided by three is minus two under the standard and minus three under flooring, and the negative-divisor case; the other two establish the result type and quotient but say nothing about the direction. No fixture computes an expected value with MOD, MODULO, FLOOR, CEILING, INT or NINT for division, or with TRIM, INDEX, REPEAT or LEN_TRIM for concatenation, and expected values are hand-computed literal constants. Table 10.4 was verified row by row because extraction interleaves columns. Two facets were correctly left pending because nondefault character kinds are processor dependent and a mixed-kind concatenation is a diagnostic boundary rather than a runtime effect. The integrator reproduced both compiler runs before recording any adjudication: thirteen of thirteen pass under the frozen LFortran 0.65.0-411-ga0afaa840b-dirty and thirteen of thirteen under gfortran 16.1.0 with -std=f2023, which reports agreement on thirteen of thirteen cases. Compiler consensus is not an oracle; the hand arithmetic was verified independently and would have overridden both had they disagreed. No LFortran gap was observed. This establishes integer division and character concatenation semantics only, and nothing about real or complex arithmetic, nondefault character kinds, or mixed-kind concatenation. All remaining pending facets, unresolved units, the retained needs-oracle real-BOZ block and every global gate remain open.
